thread:
Maria Chen: @here Incident alert — increased 5xxs and latency for Dedicated pool in us-west-2. Paging on-call now. Observed spike at ~07:12 UTC. Affects customers using pinned model v3-large.
SRE Bot: AUTOMATED: Incident created (INC-2026-1789). Paging on-call: @jonah. CPU/GPUs showing high memory pressure on pool-redwood-dedicated-3.
Jonah Park: oncall here — looking. Can someone drop the recent autoscaler policy?
Emily Rivera: I can do a quick rollback of the autoscaler policy to the previous stable threshold. Doing it now: `redwoodctl autoscaler set pool-redwood-dedicated-3 --min 2 --max 24 --policy stable-2026-01`
Jonah Park: ack. Also seeing a bunch of KV cache eviction errors in the runtime logs, looks like eviction thrash -> OOM spikes -> transient process restarts.
Priya Nair: hmm that lines up with a config change we pushed yesterday to eviction aggressiveness for cost optimization.
Alex G.: Can we enable fallback routing to the quantized variant to reduce memory? `policy: fallback:model-quant-v3` — that should avoid restarts but may increase latency.
Jonah Park: yes enable fallback now, and Emily proceed with autoscaler rollback.
Emily Rivera: fallback enabled. rolling counts show traffic shifting to model-quant-v3. 503s down from 9% -> 2% in the last 3m. Latency for some p95s increased ~120ms but error rate improving.
Maria Chen: quick customer-impact check: affected customers list from billing tags shows 8 active dedicated tenants with pinned v3-large in us-west-2. Two of them reported errors via support. We should draft status page and customer notification.
Jonah Park: root-cause hypothesis: eviction aggressiveness change + autoscaler thresholds too narrow caused memory pressure -> worker restarts -> request failures. Short-term mitigations: rollback eviction config, autoscaler rollback, fallback routing to quantized model. Medium: revert the eviction change and add headroom in autoscaler policy. Long-term: add memory-pressure alerts and circuit-breaker before eviction thrash.
Priya Nair: noted — I'll open a config rollback PR and flag for urgent review. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/configs/pull/3221
Maria Chen: Drafting status page (short):
- Maria Chen: `Status: Degraded performance and 5xx errors for Dedicated inference in us-west-2. Mitigation: autoscaler and eviction config rollback in progress; fallback routing enabled. Impact: subset of Dedicated customers pinned to v3-large may have experienced failed requests or higher latency. ETA next update: 20 minutes.`
Jonah Park: add note about mitigation: `Temporary fallback to quantized model active to reduce error rate.`
Emily Rivera: posting status page update now (draft):
```
[Statuspage] Degraded - Dedicated inference (us-west-2)
We are investigating increased error rates and latency affecting Dedicated pools. Mitigations underway: autoscaler rollback and temporary fallback to quantized model. A subset of customers with pinned models may see errors or higher latency.
Current ETA for next update: 20 minutes.
```
Maria Chen: Also prepping customer notification template: short, proactive, and technical enough for enterprise contacts.
- Maria Chen: `Hi <Customer>, we observed increased errors and latency for Dedicated inference in us-west-2 between 07:12–07:40 UTC impacting requests to pinned model v3-large. We have applied a rollback to autoscaler and eviction settings and enabled a temporary fallback to a quantized variant to restore availability. If you continue to see issues please reply and we will prioritize. A post-incident summary with root cause and preventative actions will follow.`
Priya Nair: Looks good — recommend adding whether any data exposure occurred (none expected). Add: `No customer data was exfiltrated or exposed; this was a resource management/regression issue.`
Alex G.: Also include an ops contact and incident number.
Maria Chen: Sending to the two affected customer CSMs for review before sending.
Jonah Park: Current next steps for SRE: finish eviction rollback PR, monitor memory and restart rates for 2h, add temporary alert for memory-thrash, and schedule follow-up postmortem.
Emily Rivera: eviction rollback merged and deployed at 07:28 UTC — observed worker restarts drop to baseline. Monitoring continues.
SRE Bot: AUTOMATED: Incident status changed to Mitigated at 07:34 UTC. Incident INC-2026-1789.
Maria Chen: Good job team. We'll compile a post-incident customer follow-up in this thread once we have timeline + RCA. Everyone please add one-line notes of what you did for the RCA doc.
Jonah Park: one-line: Investigated OOM/restart pattern, enabled fallback routing, coordinated autoscaler rollback, confirmed mitigations reduced 5xxs.
Emily Rivera: one-line: rolled back autoscaler to stable thresholds, deployed eviction rollback, monitored health metrics.
Priya Nair: one-line: authored rollback PR for eviction config and validated config anomalies from yesterday's deploy.
Alex G.: one-line: suggested and enabled fallback to quantized model; validated request success rates improved.
Maria Chen: Draft RCA summary for customers (short):
`Between 07:12–07:34 UTC on 2026-05-08, a configuration change to eviction aggressiveness combined with autoscaler thresholds caused memory pressure in a Dedicated GPU pool, leading to worker restarts and increased 5xx errors for customers pinned to model v3-large in us-west-2. Immediate mitigations (autoscaler rollback, eviction rollback, and temporary fallback to quantized model) were applied and restored service. No customer data was exposed. Preventative actions: revert the eviction change, add autoscaler headroom, add memory-thrash alerts and a circuit-breaker to avoid evictions under pressure.`
Maria Chen: Will send the RCA draft to CS and legal for review, aim to send to customers by EOD. Closing notes: make sure we update runbook to include this autoscaler + eviction interaction.
Emily Rivera: I'll update the runbook PR after postmortem.
Maria Chen: Thanks all. Closing thread once customer notifications go out. :white_check_mark:
